es-080h.title: Landscape: arid, very sandy soil
es-080h.summary: In the southeast, especially Murcia, a rather arid landscape with very sandy soil and medium-size mountains around. Small shrubs and small fruit or olive plantations are common by rural roads.

es-0bDx.title: Sign: hunting signs
es-0bDx.summary: Rural hunting signs, unique here: a plain white one reading "coto ... caza", or one split diagonally black and white. A readable code on it can show the region ("Ex" is Extremadura).

es-0hzs.title: Bus stops: round-topped red stops, green buses
es-0hzs.summary: Around the capital, bus stops have round red tops and buses are green. Some stops are just a red post. In the city centre buses are blue.

es-11lN.title: Buildings: big square granary on four pillars
es-11lN.summary: In Asturias, hórreos are bigger, usually square and on four pillars, with or without walls. A rectangular version on six or eight pillars is called a panera. A slate roof means western Asturias.

es-15qx.title: Language: Spanish, ñ, de and del
es-15qx.summary: Closely related to Portuguese. Ñ only exists in Spanish; Ç and lh are Portuguese (Ç is also Catalan). Portuguese uses -ao endings and -nh- instead of ñ, and contracts de to da, do, das, dos. Regional languages are covered separately.

differs.how: Portuguese has ç, lh, -ão, -nh- and da/do/dos

es-20Je.title: Pole: upside-down triangle top, upturned bar
es-20Je.summary: "French style" pole tops shaped like an upside-down triangle with a slightly upward-curved top bar, on tall ladder poles or mid-size steel poles. Also very common in France.

es-2KLU.title: Towns: all-white houses on a mountainside
es-2KLU.summary: Towns of entirely white houses built on a mountain face are very common on the south coast around Málaga.

es-3rNS.title: Pole: yellow snow poles with one or two
es-3rNS.summary: Yellow snow poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias, usually in the south of the region.

es-4F9m.title: Sign: white direction signs with coloured road
es-4F9m.summary: White direction signs, often with colourful boxes showing road numbers in many colours. Highway signs are blue.

es-4Xxl.title: Chevron: black or blue with white arrows
es-4Xxl.summary: Two chevrons: black with white arrows and blue with white arrows. Single-arrow chevrons are rare. Black-white ones also exist in Italy, Greece and Albania, blue-white only in France, and Portugal uses black with yellow.

differs.how: Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows

es-4l5N.title: Language: Galician, ñ but no ç
es-4l5N.summary: A Romance language close to Portuguese, less dominant than Catalan, so many signs are Spanish only. Galician uses ñ and has no ç, which helps tell it from Portuguese.

differs.how: Portuguese has ç and no ñ

es-5Z5E.title: Plants: orange groves on open flat land
es-5Z5E.summary: In the Guadalquivir basin, many orange plantations on much more open and flat land than on the east coast. Some are in the mountains, but coverage is sparse there.

es-6msN.title: Field markers: stone with blue left half
es-6msN.summary: In Castilla la Mancha, stone markers with the regional coat of arms line fields. They are recognisable from afar by the blue left side and unpainted right side.

es-7JxR.title: Towns: whole towns of white-painted houses
es-7JxR.summary: In the centre and south, towns made fully of white houses are very common in Andalucía and Extremadura. Castilla la Mancha has many white houses too, but streets where every house is white are uncommon.

es-7jLe.title: Town names: begin with A, O, As or Os
es-7jLe.summary: Many town names start with A, O, As or Os ("A Pena", "O Burgo", "As Cruces"). This is common and unique to the north-west, and rarely over the border in western Asturias.

es-9frM.title: Landscape: snowy peaks November to May
es-9frM.summary: The Sierra Nevada has snowy peaks from November through May, and is the only range in the south with snow most of the year.

es-ATBx.title: Landscape: extremely flat delta
es-ATBx.summary: The Ebro delta (Deltebre) is extremely flat with rice fields and water canals. Big mountains lie to the south, west and north, and some can be seen from nearly everywhere.

es-B90V.title: Houses: fully white
es-B90V.summary: The typical Balearic house is painted completely white. Flat roofs exist, but low-pitched tiled roofs are the most common.

es-Boq6.title: Plants: Mediterranean maritime pine
es-Boq6.summary: The Mediterranean variant has grey bark with red tones, usually deeply fissured. Found in most central and southern mountain ranges, with big plantations on flat ground north of Segovia.

es-C47E.title: Plants: maritime pine, grey-red bark
es-C47E.summary: Near the Atlantic coast, maritime pines have grey bark with red undertones and fluffy upward-pointing branches, and older trees have no branches in the lower half. Plantations are extremely common in north and central Portugal.

es-CAu9.title: Road numbers: letter codes show the region
es-CAu9.summary: Regional road numbers carry region codes on markers and sometimes direction signs (for example SG is one province). National roads use E, AP, A, R, N anywhere. A is also used for regional roads in two regions. See the infographic for all codes.

es-COji.title: Landscape: very diverse, forests to semi-desert
es-COji.summary: Highly varied: lush forests to bone-dry semi-desert, high plateaus with rolling hills, jagged mountains and very flat lowlands.

es-Ci25.title: Landscape: low coastal shrubs
es-Ci25.summary: Formentera often shows low coastal shrubs, and the mountains of Ibiza can often be seen from its north coast.

es-D6m4.title: Houses: big concrete blocks
es-D6m4.summary: Many houses in Galicia are built with big concrete blocks, sometimes textured like natural stone. Plain concrete blocks are also very common for walls and garages.

es-DSs8.title: Road lines: outer line style
es-DSs8.summary: On small roads without a centre line, edge-line style is a strong region clue. Where solid edges prevail, dashed ones are very rare. Where dashed prevail, solid ones are rare but less so. Some provinces have their own style, such as simple long dashed centre lines in Araba, or long outer dashes on roads with a centre line in Gipuzkoa.

es-DtCL.title: Landscape: very arid, little plants
es-DtCL.summary: Fuerteventura is very arid with almost no vegetation. Orange soil is common and essentially unique to this island among the Canaries.

es-EBga.title: Plants: stone pine, fluffy, wide bulbous crown
es-EBga.summary: Stone pines have fluffy leaves and a compact bulb-shaped crown wider than tall. Pure stone pine forests on flat land are common around Valladolid and Huelva, and they appear in residential mountain areas near Barcelona.

es-EV7o.title: Buildings: narrow raised granary (horreo)
es-EV7o.summary: In Galicia, unique raised granaries called horreos gallegos or cabazos are very common. They can be of different materials but always have the same shape.

es-EW4H.title: Guardrail: black and white
es-EW4H.summary: Within Spain, black and white guardrails are found only in Ceuta.

es-EYsT.title: Road: rectangular or square km markers
es-EYsT.summary: Most kilometre markers are rectangular or square, which can rule out half the country. Some unique designs: very tall ones with an extra stripe naming the road authority in Andalusia, square ones with the regional flag at the top in Madrid, and larger ones with a semicircle top in Biscay. National roads always have a red rectangular marker.

es-FDKM.title: Landscape: green lush hills, hedges and meadows
es-FDKM.summary: The far north is much greener and lusher than the rest, generally hilly, with hedges and green meadows. Some places look a bit like Ireland, France or the UK.

es-FT9W.title: Plants: open fields with scattered holm and
es-FT9W.summary: Open fields sparsely dotted with small holm oaks and cork oaks, very common in Extremadura and nearby. They look Mediterranean and can resemble olive trees at first glance. North of Cáceres it is lusher and winter and spring coverage is more common.

es-GGQR.title: Sign: very ornate decorated frame street name
es-GGQR.summary: Bilbao uses a street sign with a very elaborately decorated frame, found nowhere else in the country.

es-Ghny.title: Bollard: standard with green top
es-Ghny.summary: In Extremadura the normal Spanish bollards often have green tops, a variant unique to the region.

es-GkGj.title: Plants: endless olive groves on rolling hills
es-GkGj.summary: Around Córdoba and Jaén, massive olive plantations spread over rolling hills as far as the eye can see. The bigger, more remote ones are usually only covered in Gen 2.

es-H1IB.title: Flags: regional flags are common
es-H1IB.summary: Regional flags are fairly common, so they are worth learning.

es-H9Dc.title: Bus stops: red post with CTA logo
es-H9Dc.summary: Most bus stops in Asturias have a red post with the CTA logo on top. Madrid bus stops can be red too, but the operator there is EMT.

es-HdDf.title: Walls: low rock walls everywhere
es-HdDf.summary: Low rock walls are extremely common on the Balearic Islands. The area around Bari in Italy has a similar amount and can look alike.

differs.how: Bari area has similar walls and can look alike

es-Hrj7.title: Plants: Aleppo pine, fluffy, messy crown
es-Hrj7.summary: Aleppo pines are fluffy too, but their crown is looser, messier and often taller than a stone pine's. The most common pine on the east coast and Balearic Islands.

es-IRH5.title: Sign: hunting sign "Àrea privada de Caça"
es-IRH5.summary: In Catalonia and sometimes the Balearic Islands, hunting signs in Catalan, usually "Àrea privada de Caça".

es-IsPo.title: Bollard: flat with square red reflector
es-IsPo.summary: The AP-15 in Navarra has unique simple flat bollards with a square red reflector, and guardrails there have red reflectors unlike the rest of the country.

es-JLZT.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing with 8 stripes
es-JLZT.summary: A crossing sign with 8 stripes, the most in Europe and almost unique to Spain. Andorra is the only other European country with 8.

es-JhZA.title: Landscape: flat farmland, cereals, sunflowers
es-JhZA.summary: The centre of Castilla y León is mostly flat farmland with slight height changes. Most fields grow wheat and barley, and sunflower fields are fairly common.

es-JopK.title: Camera: weird low-quality, wide round blur
es-JopK.summary: A strange low-quality camera (the Ari, or "shitcam") with a wide round car blur, no sky halo (which Gen 2 has) and often brownish colours. Good maps usually exclude it, but know it exists.

es-LcNX.title: Road: km marker with orange
es-LcNX.summary: Kilometre markers have a coloured border: standard colours are orange, green and yellow from bigger to smaller roads. Some regions and provinces use different colours or designs.

es-MxpO.title: Roofs: almost black slate roofs
es-MxpO.summary: A large part of the north-west has almost only slate roofs (nearly black). They reach the west coast of Galicia but stop abruptly in the east. Slate roofs also appear in the Pyrenees near Andorra and in the mountains northeast of Madrid.

differs.how: Slate roofs appear near Andorra in the Pyrenees too

es-NHoP.title: Language: "carrer" means street
es-NHoP.summary: The Catalan word for street is carrer. Seeing it instead of calle means a Catalan-speaking region (the north-east, Valencia or the Balearic Islands). Andorra uses Catalan too.

es-Npdc.title: Landscape: dark exposed volcanic soil
es-Npdc.summary: On Lanzarote, very dark, bare volcanic soil that can look like the moon. Other Canary islands can look similar, but it is by far the most common here.

es-NrMX.title: Taxi: black with yellow doors
es-NrMX.summary: Taxis in Barcelona are black with yellow doors, including the trunk door.

es-NyOz.title: Sign: "Rúa" with accent for street
es-NyOz.summary: Streets are commonly "Rúa" in this region, while Portugal writes "Rua" without an accent. Signs without the accent can still appear here.

differs.how: Portugal writes Rua without the accent

es-OutB.title: Plants: vineyards between mountain ranges
es-OutB.summary: Vineyards appear in several places, but vineyards between mountain ranges to the north and south mean La Rioja.

es-Ozxq.title: Islands: archipelago off west Africa
es-Ozxq.summary: The Canary Islands are a Spanish archipelago off the west coast of Africa, far from the mainland, so recognising them matters for your score. Don't confuse them with the Portuguese Azores and Madeira.

differs.how: Azores and Madeira are Portuguese island groups nearby

es-PXQL.title: Rubbish bins: COGERSA logo
es-PXQL.summary: Trash containers in Asturias often carry the COGERSA logo, a distinct shape visible from far away. Recycling bins can have it too.

es-Pfi5.title: Sign: "Vado permanente" no-parking at garages
es-Pfi5.summary: No-parking signs in front of garage doors and gates read "Vado permanente", often with the municipality after "Ayuntamiento de". Italy's say "Passo carrabile".

es-Pgs1.title: Landscape: very mountainous
es-Pgs1.summary: A very mountainous country. The highest ranges are in the northeast and southeast. A high, mostly flat plateau sits in the centre, ringed by smaller ranges, with two more ranges inside. Four big river basins matter: two cross Extremadura into Portugal, one covers southwest Andalusia, and one flows into the Mediterranean in the south of Catalonia.

es-Pohw.title: Plants: orange groves in small valleys
es-Pohw.summary: Many orange plantations on the east coast, usually in small valleys. On flat land you can usually see mountains to the west, north or south.

es-Pptg.title: Chevron: big square, single arrow
es-Pptg.summary: Big square chevrons with a single arrow are common in Catalonia.

es-Pr6E.title: Road lines: dashed outer lines on rural roads
es-Pr6E.summary: Rural roads sometimes have dashed outer lines, which are almost nonexistent in Portugal and Italy. But many roads here have solid outer lines too, so only the dashed type is a clue.

differs.how: Dashed outer lines are almost nonexistent there
Dashed outer lines are almost nonexistent there

es-QsFO.title: Bollard: squarer orange reflector
es-QsFO.summary: Extremely common in Las Palmas province (Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, Lanzarote): a squarer orange reflector on the front and a white reflector at the back instead of two dots. Also in Lleida and Tarragona on the mainland. Tenerife province only has standard bollards, on highways.

es-RAmj.title: Google car: Gen 3 antenna with white top
es-RAmj.summary: A special Gen 3 antenna with a white top, like Gibraltar's, in the eastern half of Andalusia and the provinces of Huesca and Lleida.

es-RGJT.title: Sign: yellow scallop shell on blue
es-RGJT.summary: The Camino de Santiago pilgrim routes are marked with a yellow scallop on blue, on traffic signs and waystones. Pilgrims often hike or bike here, especially in summer. Markers exist across Europe, even Lithuania, but are far more common near Santiago de Compostela.

differs.how: Markers appear there but are much rarer

es-RiC9.title: Phone numbers: landlines start 9 plus region
es-RiC9.summary: Area codes are very useful: two digits give a very accurate guess. Landlines start with 9 followed by the regional digits. Mobiles start with 6 and don't help.

es-SBbI.title: Plants: tall thin pine, dark bark
es-SBbI.summary: Scots pines are tall and thin, with dark bark that sheds near the top to show orange-red wood, and no branches on the lower half of the trunk when mature. Found mainly in the Pyrenees, the Sierra de Guadarrama and the Iberian System.

es-Sxg8.title: Sign: green or blue top strip with municipality
es-Sxg8.summary: Towns often use signs with a green or blue strip at the top showing the municipality name. "Concello" is the word for municipality and is exclusive to the region.

es-TrLp.title: Landscape: semi-desert strip, light sand
es-TrLp.summary: A strip of semi-desert on both sides of the Ebro basin, from Navarra across the middle of Aragón, with light sandy soil and small shrubs on small hills.

es-TrmZ.title: Houses: flat roofs in warm pale yellow to red
es-TrmZ.summary: Ceuta has north African architecture: mostly flat-roofed houses in warm colours from pale yellow to red. Almost all Gen 4 coverage has a bright blue sky in sunny weather with occasional clouds.

es-Ug5F.title: Sign: government signs with green stripe on
es-Ug5F.summary: Signs from the Andalusian regional government have a green stripe on the left. Small versions on green signposts often mark nature reserves.

es-VJKm.title: Coverage: rare unique car in a national park
es-VJKm.summary: In Doñana National Park, southwest of Seville, there is a rare and unique car.

es-WihJ.title: Landscape: grazing fields on one island
es-WihJ.summary: Within the Balearic Islands, grazing fields are almost exclusive to Menorca.

es-XXLv.title: Landscape: dry coastal pine hills
es-XXLv.summary: A coastal Mediterranean look: somewhat dry Aleppo pine forests on most hills, with small patches of farmland (mainly fruit and olive trees) on flatter ground between towns.

es-Y8q6.title: Language: Catalan, i for and, à è ò, ç
es-Y8q6.summary: A Romance language close to Spanish and French, much more common than Spanish on signs on the north-east coast and islands, more mixed in Valencia. Catalan uses i for "and" (Spanish y), grave accents à è ò, and ç, none of which Spanish uses.

es-aLWf.title: Power: many big pylons with high-voltage lines
es-aLWf.summary: High-voltage lines on pylons are very common, even compared with other Mediterranean countries.

es-b7or.title: Plants: vines in volcanic soil behind
es-b7or.summary: Unique vineyards in volcanic soil with semicircular rock walls, on Lanzarote.

es-bPCs.title: Plate: long white, one blue strip on left
es-bPCs.summary: Standard long white European plates with a single blue strip on the left. Portuguese plates mostly have a yellow strip on the right, and Italian plates have two blue strips, one on each side.

es-bzWl.title: Greenhouses: many white-roofed greenhouses
es-bzWl.summary: Between Almería and Motril, many greenhouses with white roofs on lowland by the sea, especially around El Ejido.

es-ckbR.title: Pole: blue and yellow snow poles
es-ckbR.summary: Blue and yellow snow poles are unique to Andalusia.

es-d6lH.title: Bollard: short flat white stick
es-d6lH.summary: Common on regional roads in Aragón: a short, flat, rectangular white bollard with a grey reflector on both sides. Similar ones exist elsewhere but are far less frequent.

es-df4l.title: Landscape: light grey rock, pines, rock walls
es-df4l.summary: A big mountain range on the French border with some of the highest peaks, light grey rock, many pines and local buildings with rock walls. Andorra and the French side look very similar, and the exclave of Llívia is Spanish.

es-ejSh.title: Camera: low smallcam
es-ejSh.summary: Some Gen 4 smallcam coverage is mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small front bump. The blur can be fully transparent and hard to spot.

es-eqyH.title: Flag: unofficial red-yellow striped
es-eqyH.summary: The Catalan independence flag is unofficial but common in Catalan-speaking areas. It uses the red and yellow Senyera stripes that also appear in four regional flags.

es-gdaf.title: Language: "calle" means street
es-gdaf.summary: The Spanish word for street is calle.

es-iLYe.title: Chevron: small square, red arrow on white
es-iLYe.summary: Small square chevrons with a red arrow on white exist only in Murcia.

es-k10w.title: Coverage: two exclaves in North Africa
es-k10w.summary: Two Spanish enclaves in North Africa, partly surrounded by Morocco, have coverage. They often surprise new players, so know they exist.

es-k4DO.title: Landscape: mountainous Mediterranean
es-k4DO.summary: A mountainous Mediterranean landscape with a mix of eucalyptus and pines in Ceuta.

es-kVqr.title: Plants: olives in small or medium fields
es-kVqr.summary: South of Madrid, olive plantations are usually in small or medium fields on mostly flat ground, often with red soil.

es-kZ8q.title: Google car: black, no antenna
es-kZ8q.summary: In Asturias, a black car with no antenna and a visible brake light. It can very rarely spill into neighbouring regions like Galicia.

es-kpT2.title: Landscape: barren island, always overcast
es-kpT2.summary: The small island of La Graciosa, off Lanzarote's north coast, is completely barren and all coverage is overcast. Two towns on the south coast have white flat-roofed houses like the eastern Canaries.

es-lFNR.title: Sign: bilingual sub-signs with thick black
es-lFNR.summary: Road signs in the Basque Country and Navarre often have bilingual sub-signs with a thick black border. Basque is usually on top in the Basque Country, Spanish usually on top in Navarre.

es-lQAo.title: Sign: "Gual permanent" no-parking
es-lQAo.summary: In Catalan-speaking areas no-parking signs read "Gual permanent". Most municipalities in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands use "gual", while Valencia mixes Spanish and Catalan.

es-lRNZ.title: Pole: steel mesh with rectangles, not triangles
es-lRNZ.summary: Poles whose steel mesh forms rectangles instead of the usual triangles, in the southern half, especially Murcia and southern Alicante.

es-lZxf.title: Sign: red borders reach the edge of road signs
es-lZxf.summary: The red border of road signs goes right to the sign's edge, with no thin white outer border. France, Italy and Portugal have a small white edge.

es-lm-2236.title: Language: ñ, ¿ ¡, y, -ción, -miento, ll
es-lm-2236.summary: Ñ is almost unique to Spanish (Galician aside). Inverted ¿ ¡ are common, "and" is y, and common words are de, el, del, los, la, uno, una. Endings: -o, -a, -ción, -miento, -dad. Double ll is more common than in other Romance languages (except Catalan).

es-lm-2238.title: Language: handy words like estación
es-lm-2238.summary: Useful Spanish words: centro ciudad (city centre), estación (station), iglesia (church), excepto (except), aparcamiento (parking), salida (exit), parque (park), todas direcciones (all directions), se vende (for sale), se alquila (for rent).

es-lm-2239.title: Language: street words calle, avenida, camino
es-lm-2239.summary: Street words: calle (street), pasaje (alley), avenida (avenue), camino (way or path), carretera (highway).

es-lm-558163.title: Sign: each street name in its own section
es-lm-558163.summary: Seville street signs have each name in its own section in a distinctive font.

es-lm-558167.title: Sign: white street name, leaf-like blue frame
es-lm-558167.summary: Zaragoza street signs are white with a unique logo in the top left and a fancy decorated blue frame that looks a bit like leaves.

es-lm-558168.title: Sign: street name with logo in top left
es-lm-558168.summary: Valencia street signs have a unique logo in the top left.

es-lm-558225.title: Sign: picture street names or blue with crown
es-lm-558225.summary: Madrid has two kinds: in the centre each sign has a different picture; outside the centre they are blue with white text and a logo on the left that looks like a crown over something. Check for the crown, as there are slightly different versions.

es-lm-742376.title: Sign: blue street name, thick white edge
es-lm-742376.summary: Murcia street signs are blue with a thick white edge and a unique logo with a crown on the left.

es-lm-840.title: Language: Aranese, carrèr, avenguda, passeg
es-lm-840.summary: Spoken by about 2,800 people in Val d'Aran, looking very similar to Catalan. Street names are the easiest clue: carrèr (Catalan carrer, with the accent on e), avenguda (avinguda), passeg (passeig). It is mountainous with many rock buildings like Andorra.

differs.how: Similar mountains and rock houses, but Aranese spellings differ

es-ln7z.title: Houses: isolated stone farmhouses (masías)
es-ln7z.summary: Traditional stone farmhouses called masías, standing alone or in a small group, are common in Catalonia, eastern Aragón and parts of Valencia.

es-m1NG.title: Houses: north African style, hazy and overcast
es-m1NG.summary: Melilla has similar north African architecture. Its coverage looks hazy with a much less saturated sky than Ceuta and is mostly cloudy or overcast. There is little rural coverage, mainly by the Morocco border.

es-mAZ9.title: Landscape: dry Mediterranean most places
es-mAZ9.summary: There is no single landscape, but most of the country has a fairly dry Mediterranean climate with matching plants and crops.

es-mvou.title: Plants: fenced olive groves or behind rock
es-mvou.summary: On the east coast, olive plantations are often fenced or behind rock walls, and you almost always see mountains in some direction.

es-ni44.title: Google car: blue or black Gen 4
es-ni44.summary: Newer Gen 4 cars are blue or, less often, black. The car can be completely hidden.

es-oE35.title: Sign: road marker with colourful border
es-oE35.summary: Distinct road markers with colourful borders, with the road number in the code on top. Andorra has similar markers, and the letters before the number are a key region clue.

es-oi9R.title: Plants: olive trees across half the country
es-oi9R.summary: Olive trees are one of the main crops and can be seen in more than half of the country.

es-okgv.title: Guardrail: yellow reflectors on rounded A-type
es-okgv.summary: Yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails. Belgium, Andorra, Gibraltar and most Latin American countries have yellow reflectors too.

es-pPsk.title: Plants: eucalyptus plantations
es-pPsk.summary: Eucalyptus plantations are found all along the north coast, with more in Galicia than in the rest of the north combined. Also extremely common in Portugal.

es-pS3a.title: Plants: eucalyptus in dry land
es-pS3a.summary: Eucalyptus trees in a dry setting most likely mean Huelva province. They are rarer in Extremadura to the north and as far east as Córdoba.

es-pq0v.title: Landscape: very diverse, volcanic, pines, arid
es-pq0v.summary: Extremely varied: steep mountains, pine forests, volcanic soil and extreme dryness, though some places look like mainland Spain. Look for something that feels off compared with mainland Europe even when the other clues say Spain.

es-pz9i.title: Landscape: very arid, mostly flat
es-pz9i.summary: Very dry, mostly flat land in central and south Aragón. Soil is very white and rocky in the north and redder around Teruel.

es-qBpO.title: Pole: concrete ladder or wooden in rural areas
es-qBpO.summary: Many pole types exist. In small towns and sparse rural areas, concrete ladder poles (with ladder-like indents) and wooden poles are the most common.

es-rcrC.title: Language: "kalea" for street
es-rcrC.summary: Streets in Basque-speaking areas are sometimes called "kalea", though "calle" is still common.

es-rjCb.title: Plants: thick forests of tall pines
es-rjCb.summary: Thick tall pine forests cover the mountains on the French border. In smaller mountains between grazing fields or farmland, you are most likely in the Basque Country or Navarra.

es-rzeV.title: Crops: corn in big river basins
es-rzeV.summary: Corn is mostly grown in big river basins. It also grows on the north coast, especially Galicia, and in part of north-west Castilla y León.

es-t0On.title: Sign: flat signposts on most road signs
es-t0On.summary: Almost all road signs, kilometre markers, chevrons and some direction signs sit on flat signposts. Portugal, France and Andorra have flat posts too.

es-uZlj.title: Bollard: squarer orange reflector
es-uZlj.summary: On the mainland almost only in Lleida and Tarragona: a squarer orange reflector on the front and one white reflector on the back instead of two dots. Some toll highways such as the AP-6 use it too, and so does the eastern half of the Canary Islands.

es-v8wo.title: Bollard: yellow-orange reflector
es-v8wo.summary: The standard bollard has a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots (or nothing) on the back. They are usually hollow. Very close to Andorra a slightly different bollard is used, and also in Andorra.

differs.how: Near the border a slightly different bollard is used

es-vbq8.title: Landscape: totally flat land, vineyards, olives
es-vbq8.summary: Castilla la Mancha can be completely flat, which is less common in Castilla y León. Half of the country's wine comes from here, so vineyards are common. In the western provinces of Ciudad Real and Toledo olive plantations are common, on flatter ground than in Andalusia.

es-vcUq.title: Sign: round corrugated signposts
es-vcUq.summary: Many signs in Catalonia have round, corrugated signposts, especially direction signs. Also common in the Basque Country and Balearic Islands, and any municipality may use them. Regular traffic signs keep the flat Spanish design. French signs look very similar.

es-wOmb.title: Landscape: tall mountain range to the northwest
es-wOmb.summary: The north-west of Mallorca has a tall mountain range seen from many places on the island, the only Balearic island with mountains this big.

es-woK5.title: Houses: large white with wooden frames
es-woK5.summary: Large white houses with wooden frames are common in the Basque Country, the Basque part of Navarra and Cantabria.

es-wz9Z.title: Google car: Gen 3, antenna long, short or none
es-wz9Z.summary: Older Gen 3 cars (blurrier, softer colours) can have a long, short or no antenna. The back is usually hidden, but if visible it is black or white. East Andalusia, Huesca and Lleida sometimes have a long antenna with a white tip.

es-xE7c.title: Sign: stop sign with small text
es-xE7c.summary: Stop signs use a distinctly small font. This mostly separates it from Portugal, whose stop signs have a noticeably larger font.

differs.how: Portuguese stop sign font is noticeably larger

es-yAfo.title: Language: Basque, many Z and K
es-yAfo.summary: A language unrelated to any other, spoken in the Basque Country and northern Navarre, so signs are a mix of Spanish and Basque. Z and K are common letters. Also used across the border in southwest France.

es-yHR2.title: Coverage: early-spring dirt roads, green grass
es-yHR2.summary: In north-central Castilla la Mancha, early spring coverage on dirt roads between green grassy fields and leafless vineyards on red soil is very common, especially in the north and only Gen 3. Further south similar Gen 4 coverage exists.

es-yq2C.title: Language: several regional languages
es-yq2C.summary: The most useful for the game are Catalan, Basque and Galician. Other regions like Asturias have regional languages too, but non-Spanish signs are much rarer there.

es-zUkq.title: Landscape: rugged bare mountains in haze
es-zUkq.summary: Mountains in Murcia and the south of Alicante look very distinct: rugged and mostly bare. The area is often hazy, so far mountains look like they are behind mist.
